title: Levels of Agentic Engineering - Hacker News discussion
description: Extensive HN discussion on the maturity levels of AI-assisted coding, from basic chat interfaces to autonomous agent teams. Key themes: the importance of context management, verification challenges, token economics, the gap between vibecoded prototypes and working products, and debates about whether higher autonomy levels are actually better. Discussion highlights practical concerns about validation, hallucination management, and the future of software engineering.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Experimenting with Starlette 1.0 with Claude skills
description: Deep dive into Starlette 1.0, the lightweight ASGI framework that serves as the foundation for FastAPI. Explores the framework's capabilities through interactive experimentation with Claude AI, demonstrating routing, templating with Jinja2, async database operations with aiosqlite, and real-time updates in a task management app.
author: Simon Willison

title: JavaScript Sandboxing Research
description: Comprehensive research comparing JavaScript sandboxing options for running untrusted code. Analyzes core Node.js approaches (worker_threads, node:vm, Permission Model), npm packages (isolated-vm, vm2), and alternative engines like quickjs-emscripten.
author: Simon Willison

title: Ask HN: How is AI-assisted coding going for you professionally?
description: Hacker News thread with 577 comments sharing professional experiences with AI-assisted coding. Developers discuss their workflows, productivity gains, challenges with hallucinations, trust issues, and the balance between manual oversight and AI autonomy.
author: Hacker News Community

title: The 100 hour gap between a vibecoded prototype and a working product
description: Article discussed on Hacker News about the significant effort required to transform AI-generated prototypes into production-ready software. Highlights the difference between rapid AI prototyping and the engineering work needed for reliability, security, and scalability.
author: Macbudkowski

title: LLM Architecture Gallery
description: Comprehensive gallery of LLM architectures by Sebastian Raschka, discussed on Hacker News. Provides visual explanations and comparisons of different language model architectures, serving as a valuable educational resource for understanding LLM design patterns.
author: Sebastian Raschka

title: Chrome DevTools MCP (Model Context Protocol)
description: Chrome DevTools introduces MCP support in 2025, enabling AI agents to interact with browser DevTools programmatically. Discussed on HN as a significant step towards agent debugging capabilities. Allows automated debugging, performance analysis, and web inspection through AI agents.
author: Chrome DevTools Team

title: Profiling Hacker News users based on their comments
description: Demonstrates how LLMs can create detailed user profiles from 1,000 Hacker News comments using the Algolia Hacker News API. Raises questions about privacy and AI surveillance capabilities with public comment data.
author: Simon Willison

title: Using Git with coding agents
description: Part of the Agentic Engineering Patterns series. Explains how Git is essential for working with coding agents - recording changes, investigating mistakes, and leveraging Git's full capabilities through AI assistance.
author: Simon Willison

title: Turbo Pascal 3.02A deconstructed with AI
description: Used Claude to analyze and decompile the 39,731-byte Turbo Pascal 3.02 executable from 1985, creating an interactive artifact that maps the binary memory, shows decompiled assembly, and reconstructs readable code with annotations. Demonstrates AI's ability to interpret legacy binaries.
author: Simon Willison

title: Thoughts on OpenAI acquiring Astral and uv/ruff/ty
description: In-depth analysis of OpenAI's acquisition of Astral (company behind uv, ruff, and ty Python tools). Discusses competitive dynamics with Anthropic, strategic implications for Python ecosystem, and potential risks of single-company control over critical infrastructure.
author: Simon Willison

title: Autoresearching Apple's 'LLM in a Flash' to run Qwen 397B locally
description: Highlights Dan Woods' research running Qwen3.5-397B-A17B at 5.5+ tokens/second on a 48GB MacBook Pro M3 Max using techniques from Apple's 'LLM in a flash' paper. The Mixture-of-Experts model streams expert weights from SSD, allowing 209GB model to run with only 5.5GB in memory. Used Claude Code with Andrej Karpathy's autoresearch pattern to run 90 experiments.
author: Simon Willison

title: Snowflake Cortex AI sandbox escape
description: Reports on a PromptArmor analysis of a prompt injection attack in Snowflake's Cortex Agent. The attack exploited process substitution in shell commands, demonstrating limitations of allow-list based command pattern security in agent tools. Advocates for deterministic sandboxes outside the agent layer.
author: Simon Willison

title: Subagents in Agentic Engineering
description: Part of the Agentic Engineering Patterns series. Explains how subagents provide a simple but effective way to handle larger tasks without burning through the coding agent's valuable context. Covers parallel execution and context management.
author: Simon Willison

title: Release: llm 0.29
description: Release of version 0.29 of llm, Simon's command-line tool for accessing large language models.
author: Simon Willison

title: Introducing Mistral Small 4 and Leanstral
description: Covers Mistral's new Apache 2 licensed 119B parameter Mixture-of-Experts model (6B active) that unifies Magistral (reasoning), Pixtral (multimodal), and Devstral (agentic coding) capabilities. Also mentions Leanstral, an open weight model tuned for Lean 4 formally verifiable coding language.
author: Simon Willison

title: Coding agents for data analysis
description: Handout from NICAR 2026 workshop demonstrating how tools like Claude Code and OpenAI Codex can explore, analyze, and clean data. Workshop used GitHub Codespaces, Python, SQLite, and Datasette. Highlight: AI-generated interactive heat map visualizations.
author: Simon Willison

title: Leanstral: Open-source agent for trustworthy coding and formal proof engineering
description: Mistral AI releases Leanstral, the first open-source code agent for Lean 4 formal verification. Released with Apache 2.0 license and free API endpoint. Designed for formal proof engineering in realistic repositories, representing a shift from AI code generation to AI code verification. Available as agent mode within Mistral Vibe.
author: Mistral AI
